WITH
order_spend AS (
    -- Sum split payments before counting orders; payment_value is the amount paid.
    SELECT order_id, ROUND(SUM(payment_value), 2) AS amount_paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
customer_totals AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_purchase,
           COUNT(*) AS order_count,
           -- A missing payment record is unknown spend, not a zero-value order.
           CASE WHEN COUNT(p.amount_paid) = COUNT(*)
                THEN ROUND(SUM(p.amount_paid), 2) END AS total_spend
    FROM orders AS o
    JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN order_spend AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
rfm_values AS (
    SELECT customer_totals.*,
           -- Whole elapsed days from the customer's last purchase to the latest
           -- purchase timestamp among all delivered orders (not the delivery date).
           CAST(JULIANDAY(MAX(last_purchase) OVER ()) - JULIANDAY(last_purchase)
                AS INTEGER) AS recency_days
    FROM customer_totals
),
percentiles AS (
    -- Rank best first. Ties share the upper percentile of their group, so
    -- identical order counts are never split into different frequency scores.
    SELECT rfm_values.*,
           CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY recency_days) AS rp,
           CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY order_count DESC) AS fp,
           CASE WHEN total_spend IS NOT NULL THEN
               CUME_DIST() OVER (PARTITION BY (total_spend IS NULL) ORDER BY total_spend DESC)
           END AS mp
    FROM rfm_values
),
scores AS (
    -- Each crossed 20% boundary adds one: (0, 20%] scores 1, (80%, 100%] scores 5.
    SELECT customer_unique_id, order_count, total_spend,
           1 + (rp > 0.2) + (rp > 0.4) + (rp > 0.6) + (rp > 0.8) AS r,
           1 + (fp > 0.2) + (fp > 0.4) + (fp > 0.6) + (fp > 0.8) AS f,
           1 + (mp > 0.2) + (mp > 0.4) + (mp > 0.6) + (mp > 0.8) AS m
    FROM percentiles
),
segments AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id, order_count, total_spend,
           CASE
               WHEN r = 1 AND f + m BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Champions'
               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND f + m BETWEEN 1 AND 2 THEN 'Can''t Lose Them'
               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND f + m BETWEEN 3 AND 6 THEN 'Hibernating'
               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND f + m BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'Lost'
               WHEN r IN (2, 3) AND f + m BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Loyal Customers'
               WHEN r = 3 AND f + m BETWEEN 5 AND 6 THEN 'Needs Attention'
               WHEN r = 1 AND f + m BETWEEN 7 AND 8 THEN 'Recent Users'
               WHEN (r = 1 AND f + m BETWEEN 5 AND 6)
                 OR (r = 2 AND f + m BETWEEN 5 AND 8) THEN 'Potential Loyalists'
               WHEN r = 1 AND f + m BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Price Sensitive'
               WHEN r = 2 AND f + m BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Promising'
               WHEN r = 3 AND f + m BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'About to Sleep'
           END AS rfm_segment
    FROM scores
),
averages AS (
    SELECT rfm_segment, customer_unique_id,
           total_spend / order_count AS customer_avg,
           SUM(total_spend) OVER segment / SUM(order_count) OVER segment AS segment_avg
    FROM segments
    WINDOW segment AS (PARTITION BY rfm_segment)
)
SELECT rfm_segment, customer_unique_id,
       ROUND(customer_avg, 2) AS customer_avg_sales_per_order,
       ROUND(segment_avg, 2) AS segment_avg_sales_per_order,
       ROUND(MAX(segment_avg) OVER () - segment_avg, 2) AS gap_to_highest_segment_per_order
FROM averages
ORDER BY segment_avg DESC, rfm_segment, customer_unique_id;

    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id

)

            ELSE lifespan_days / 7.0
       END AS customer_lifespan_weeks
